THE SHARED VECTORS. One file, three consumers: this package, the web front end (web-react/src/utils/productVersion.vectors.json), and the panel's Go mirror. It is COPIED rather than fetched, because a test may not reach into another module at run time.

TWO NAMESPACES, ONE CURRENT ADDRESS. A release tag is `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[.BUILD]`, and four releases were published under `release/` before the address changed; `tag_namespace` is the current one. BOTH are read, because a published tag cannot be moved and the panel still lists those four; only the current one is DERIVED, and `derive` pins that — including the case that makes it matter, where a version published under the historical namespace does NOT derive back to its own address. The legacy v0.0.1-beta forms are a third shape and are neither: `reject_tags` is where they are refused.

WHAT IT PINS IS THE SHAPE, THE ORDER AND THE ADDRESSES. The order section carries the BUILD COMPONENT pairs, which nothing covered before: the fourth segment was ignored by the comparison, so a rebuild and its base compared equal while the panel's mirror disagreed.

reject.why: a fourth segment is rejected even when it is zero
trailing separator makes an empty segment
leading separator makes an empty segment
surrounding whitespace is the caller's to trim; the parser is strict
full-width digits are not ASCII digits
the new scheme has no prerelease suffix; that is a legacy identity
no build metadata in the product version
far past the ceiling, must not overflow or truncate
the v-prefixed form is a legacy identity, never normalised into the new scheme
a tag is not a product version
a fifth segment is a different format, not something to truncate
a zero fourth segment is another spelling of 102.1.0

tags.why: the current namespace, with the build component
four segments with a build component is a published identity, so it is a tag
the historical namespace: read, never derived
the historical namespace, with the build component

reject_tags.why: a tag names a published identity, which is three segments or four with the build component
a tag names a published identity, never shorthand
the historical namespace holds published identities too
a bare product version is not a tag, under either namespace
the version inside the historical namespace is bare; the v IS the other namespace
the namespace is a lower-case v
begins with v but is not a version — a tag is an identity, not a prefix
no release line was ever published as zero
the legacy scheme, whose tag was the version itself
a prerelease is a CHANNEL, not a spelling of a published identity
a path separator in the historical namespace
a fifth segment is a different format
a fifth segment is a different format, in either namespace

derive.why: the current namespace, which is what a release about to be published gets
the build component travels with the version it names
DERIVATION DOES NOT KNOW HISTORY: 4.0.1.2 was published as release/4.0.1.2, and a caller addressing a published release carries its tag rather than deriving it
